title: Priority escalation: rapid mitigation and postmortem action bundle
creator: Ava Chen
description: Summary: Customer X reported repeated 502/504 patterns and timeouts during peak ingest windows. Root cause surfaced as a combination of edge-proxy head-of-line blocking under high multipart fanout, aggressive client retries, and slow KV cache evictions on shared hosted pools. This ticket bundles the rapid mitigation steps we shipped, the targeted hotpatch, customer communications, and a consolidated postmortem action list across Hosted/Dedicated/Private environments.
investigation_notes:
- Observability: spike in edge queue lengths correlated with upstream runtime backpressure (see dashboard link).
- Traces showed repeated client retry waves with identical idempotency tokens and no jitter, amplifying queue pressure.
- KV cache eviction thrash on shared pools during multi-tenant maintenance window increased p99 latency for warm-start models.
- Dedicated fallback route existed but was not honored for some API keys due to missing tenant priority mapping.
- No evidence of model runtime OOM. CPU/GPU metrics remained within expected ranges for affected hosts.
remediation_plan:
1) Immediate: deploy edge-proxy quick patch to introduce an early fast-fail for connections exceeding per-tenant concurrent request threshold and return 429 with Retry-After to client SDKs.
2) Roll forward: enable tenant-priority header mapping so high-touch escalated tenants route to reserved capacity or dedicated fallback.
3) SDK coordination: request SDK team to ship recommended retry-with-jitter guidance and to honor 429 Retry-After for node/python SDKs.
4) Longer term: implement per-tenant request shaping + KV prefetch for heavy multipart uploads; harden eviction policy to reduce thrash.
5) Observability: add new alert for edge queue length crossing 95th percentile and automated tenant slowpath flagging in Console.
rollout_plan:
- Hotpatch edge-proxy to canary in region-us-west-1 for 10 minutes. Monitor error rate, p95 latency, and tenant queue length.
- If stable, incrementally roll to remaining regions over 30 minutes.
- Simultaneously apply tenant-priority mapping for Customer X and one internal test tenant.
- Notify on-call and set a two-hour post-deploy observation window before marking Done.
acceptance_criteria:
- Customer X reported request success rate improved to >= 99% for synthetic repro within 1 hour of hotpatch.
- Platform-hosted 5xx incidents attributable to retry-amplified edge-queue events reduced by >= 90% for two subsequent peak windows.
- No increase in unrelated p99 latency across other tenants (>5% relative).
- SDKs updated with retry guidance and idempotency doc linked in customer comms.
postmortem_summary: Root causes: (A) request amplification from misaligned client retry semantics and missing jitter; (B) head-of-line queueing at edge-proxy due to large multipart fanout; (C) insufficient tenant isolation mapping causing escalated tenant traffic to remain on shared, contended pools. Corrective actions taken: early fast-fail patch, tenant-priority routing, SDK guidance issued. Action items remain for eviction algorithm improvements and formal SLA playbook for priority tenant routing.
action_items: ENG-512871: Implement per-tenant concurrent request quota with graceful degradation
ENG-512872: Improve KV cache eviction policy and add targeted prefetch for heavy upload paths
PM-40500: Update SLA and escalation runbook to include dedicated fallback mapping checklist
DES-2201: Add Console indicator for tenant slowpath state and priority mapping UI
ENG-512880: Extend CI load tests to simulate multi-tenant multipart fanout
customer_communication:
- Initial acknowledgement sent within 30 minutes with escalation ticket and temporary mitigation steps.
- Follow-up email after hotpatch summarizing observed improvement and planned next steps.
- Offer dedicated engineering sync and remediation timeline; proposed dates included.
- Customer asked to run SDK with new retry guidance and report any anomalies.
